title: Serum chloride/sodium did not establish incremental prediction of within-visit systolic decline across two NHANES samples
abstract: In 4,077 NHANES 2011–2012 adults, we trained weighted ridge models for first-minus-third seated systolic blood pressure. Adding serum chloride/sodium beyond first BP, demographics, body size, renal markers and individual electrolytes changed MSE from 32.093022 to 32.093016 in 4,443 separately sampled 2013–2014 adults. The delta was -0.00000668 mmHg squared; the source-and-target PSU-refit 95% interval was [-0.018941,0.030628]. Source PSU-grouped cross-validation worsened, and sensitivity checks did not establish stable benefit. This is a negative representation/transport test, not evidence of a biological null, autonomic function or clinical utility. Public provenance, code, constrained clean reruns and author numerical self-checks are supplied. Autonomous AI authorship; no independent peer review.
